Bozeman City Commission Regular Meeting

March 4, 2025 - 6:00 PM

City Hall, Commission Room, 121 N Rouse Ave, Bozeman, MT

Roll Call

Members Present:

  • Mayor Terry Cunningham - present
  • Deputy Mayor Jennifer Madgic - present
  • Commissioner Christopher Coburn - present
  • Commissioner Emma Bode - absent
  • Commissioner Joey Morrison - present

CONSENT AGENDA

1. Approve minutes of the February 18, 2025 Regular Meeting

2. Authorize renewal of janitorial services contract with Facilities Management Inc.

3. Accept donation of public art installation for Bogert Park from the Bozeman Arts Council

PUBLIC HEARING

4. Ordinance 2152: Zone Map Amendment from R-1 to R-4 at 1800 block West Babcock Street

Applicant requests zone map amendment for high-density residential development of 48 units

5. Resolution 5702: Stormwater infrastructure improvements for Oak Street corridor

Estimated project cost of $1.8M funded through stormwater utility fees

ACTION ITEMS

6. Approve interlocal agreement with Gallatin County for shared trail maintenance on Gallagator Linear Trail

7. First reading of Ordinance 2153: Amendments to Chapter 38 Unified Development Code regarding accessory dwelling units

Motions and Votes

Motion by Deputy Mayor Madgic to approve the Consent Agenda. Second by Commissioner Morrison.

The motion passed unanimously (4-0).

  • Cunningham - Aye
  • Madgic - Aye
  • Coburn - Aye
  • Morrison - Aye

Motion by Commissioner Morrison to approve Ordinance 2152, the Zone Map Amendment for West Babcock Street.

Second by Mayor Cunningham.

  • Cunningham - Aye
  • Madgic - Aye
  • Coburn - Nay
  • Morrison - Aye

The motion passed (3-1).

Motion by Commissioner Coburn to approve the interlocal agreement for Gallagator Linear Trail maintenance.

Second by Deputy Mayor Madgic.

The motion passed unanimously (4-0).

  • Cunningham - Aye
  • Madgic - Aye
  • Coburn - Aye
  • Morrison - Aye

Public Comments

Resident Sarah Mitchell stated: "The density increase on Babcock is going to overwhelm our already strained infrastructure. We need the city to invest in roads before adding more housing."

Commissioner Coburn said "I cannot support this zone map amendment without a comprehensive traffic study. Forty-eight units on a two-lane residential street is irresponsible planning."

Mayor Cunningham stated: "We have a housing crisis and must balance neighborhood concerns with the reality that people need places to live in this community."
